newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE ends week mixed on market.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE ends week mixed on market.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares were mixed on the Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) in the week ended on Friday and dealers said trade might remain stagnant until the shares begin trading on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) later this month.
A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district SOLIDERE is rebuilding -- held steady at $105.25 on the privately-operated BSM.
B shares -- issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994 -- rose slightly to $106.5 from last Friday's $106.25.

"There is still no interest in buying. Many investors are waiting for the stock to move to the bourse. They are also waiting for the 10-for-one share stock-split -- approved by SOLIDERE shareholders -- to be carried out," a dealer said.

Market sources have said SOLIDERE will move its shares to the official bourse from the BSM on September 30. The capitalisation of the BSE is less than $400 million. SOLIDERE shares will add some $2 billion to the market.
"I hope things begin to change when the shares start trading on the bourse at the end of the month," the dealer added.
Weekly turnover on the BSM fell to 40,104 shares compared to 46,551 last week and value was $4,238,562 against $4,888,974.
On the official Beirut Stock Exchange, there was trade in only one of the four listed companies, 200 Ciments Libanais shares on Friday.
Ciments Libanais rose to $1.25 from $1.2187 last week. Total turnover on the BSE last week was 12,100 shares.
There was no trade throughout the week in the shares of the three other listed firms, Eternit, Ciments Blancs and and Uniceramic.
The BLOM Stock Index (BSI) rose 0.40 percent during the week to 911.93 and the Lebanon Invest Share Price Index (LISPI) rose 0.40 percent to 82.25. Both indexes cover both markets.
